data.name: Niamh
data.gender_notes: Niamh is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Irish word 'necht' meaning 'radiant, bright' and 'fionn' meaning 'fair, white', Niamh is the name of a goddess of the Irish mythology who was described as having radiant beauty. She was also known as the goddess of fertility and the protector of the dead. The name Niamh carries the meaning “Radiant, Bright” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Niamh usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant, bright and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of radiant beauty and the protector of the dead.
data.etymology: Niamh belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Radiant, Bright.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Niamh total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
